principles.text: A gap up at the open after a weak close is 'great for the shorts' - it delivers the bounce into the declining 9/21 that the short entry needs.

Shorting a rally into prior swing lows + the 60-minute 9 EMA while the stock is very extended from the daily EMAs is an aggressive, lower-win-rate entry: only works when the market is really trending, so be very selective with it.
Skip a short when earnings are tomorrow, even if the chart is right.
When you're 50/50 on a trade, run it as an imaginary position and let the market grade it over a few days - a free test of the idea (used on the PSTG-type rejection at the hourly 9/21).

High-R/R short pattern: a wide-range candle with a long upper wick, high volume and a weak close (below the prior day's low) after a big run, followed by a gap up into the 15-minute 9/21 EMA; the fade reads as a failed breakout / upthrust. Not far from the swing high, so the stop is tight.

'This is not the right environment for taking any longs' - willing to take paper cuts and focus only on the short side while shorts have traction; even if MU takes out the prior week high, look for the failed-breakout short rather than the long.

Weakness shows up in individual names before the index: count how many stocks degrade from the leading to the mediocre to the lagging list, leaders (semis, CCJ, airlines, software) slowing, more mega caps below the 9 EMA than above, and small caps going illiquid and getting removed. The IWM breakdown is confirmation, not the trigger. Felt like late 2021 and Dec 2024/Jan 2025.

Shorting weak vs strong stocks: neither has a clear edge. A beaten-down name gives a higher win rate but less follow-through; a strong name (still above all EMAs, 'pulling back from highs') gives higher R/R with a lower win rate. Stated as an unverified take.

Progressive exposure is used much less now: tighter stops (<1% on shorts) and lower risk per trade let him size aggressively while keeping drawdowns small - three or four losses cost ~6-7% of account instead of the old 5%-risk, 2%-stop regime.
Breadth indicators (MMFI, S5FI, % of S&P above the 20/50) were tried and found less useful than browsing his own stock universe.
Can't fully reconstruct the step-by-step switch from bullish to bearish; the main trigger was Thursday's (8/27) gap up creating tons of short entries.
Tier-2 watchlist = small/micro caps under ~$5B, split at $200M dollar volume per day (more liquid ones get traded).

Same chart, opposite trade depending on market context: SNDK's current pattern would be a LONG if QQQ were 25% off its highs (Apr 2025) but is a SHORT with QQQ 4% off highs after an 8000% run. Too many technical traders look only at the price action and ignore the context.
Not a fan of buying a pullback right after a huge rejection candle (DOCS); nor buying platinum (PPLT) into prior lows with a weak weekly structure.
Crypto: wait for the pullback into the weekly 9 before buying; they can break out now but he isn't interested.
